item.title: Contributing
item.description: vex is a single LuaJIT program with no build step. This page covers working on it; Plugin architecture and Resolution pipeline explain how it fits together.

item.title: Plugin architecture
item.description:
Every swappable part of vex, including id generation, file layout, the task file format and sort order, goes through one mechanism: src/lib/plugin.lua.

Enums: named slots with one active member link

Plugin:addenum(name, members, active) registers a slot: a name, the implementations that can fill it, and the one that is active. src/vex.lua registers six:

 plugin:addenum("tagger", {"canonicalvexid"})
plugin:addenum("taskpath", {"grouppath"})
plugin:addenum("taskformat", {"obsidian"})
plugin:addenum("sortdata", {"canonicalsort"})
plugin:addenum("frontmatter", {"canonicalfrontmatter"})
plugin:addenum("body", {"canonicalbody"})

Plugin:select(name, member) switches the active member. The rest of vex depends only on the slot. Markdown with YAML frontmatter is simply what the obsidian member of taskformat writes; another member could store the same fields as JSON or database rows, and schemas, focuses and views would work unchanged.

item.title: Resolution pipeline
item.description:
How a task goes from vex add to a file on disk, and what else moves when it does. The code is TaskManager in src/core/task.lua.

add, resolve, write link

  1. TaskManager:add makes a vexid with the tagger plugin and holds the new task in memory only.
  2. TaskManager:resolve runs the schema of the task’s type and of each type it extends, from the root down. Each schema runs three steps: normalise (fill defaults, convert values), validate, and derive (compute fields, record links). A failure throws a named resolution-failed-* error and nothing is written. Resolution then indexes the task in memory and moves files into place (below).
